sentences.text: Heard Sri. Sharath J.M, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. N Anitha Girish, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent -State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner being the sole accused is seeking grant of bail.
He was apprehended on 20.06.2022 and since then, he is in judicial custody.

It is alleged that the petitioner had induced the minor girl,
Somashekar @ Prashanth vs State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167945709/
2 kidnapped her, kept her away for about 6 months and committed sexual assault repeatedly, under the guise of marrying her.

sentences.text:
The statement of the victim under Section 164 of Cr.PC was recorded,
wherein she has NC: 2024:KHC:37471 reiterated the allegations made against the petitioner.
Investigation was undertaken and the charge sheet is filed.
The medical report supports the contention of the prosecution.

Since serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence, his earlier petition Crl.P.No.11295/2022 came to be dismissed by this Court vide order dated 06.02.2023.
5.
Now the petitioner has again approached this Court to contend that the charge was framed by the Trial court on 16.03.2023.
On 24.07.2023 one of the mahazar witnesses was examined as PW-1.
Even though the prosecution has cited as many as 39 witness, none of the other witnesses have been examined till date.

6. Learned counsel also submits that on 19.04.2024, the Director of the Ashram where the victim - CW-1 was housed had lodged the missing complaint stating that the victim girl is found missing along with other minor girls.
Therefore, it is his contention that completion of the trial may not be possible in near future and therefore, the petitioner is entitled for bail.
These facts are not disputed by learned High NC: 2024:KHC:37471 Court Government Pleader, but on the other hand she admits that there is delay in examining the witnesses, since CW-1 is found missing.
Under such circumstances, detention of the petitioner in custody for indefinite period without any progress that is being made, would amount to infringement of his right to life and liberty.
No useful purpose would be served by detaining the petitioner in the custody.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled to be enlarged on bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the interest of the prosecution.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.8/2022 of Ramanagara Police Station, pending in Spl.C.C.No.101/2022 on the file of the learned I Additional District and Sessions Court, Ramanagar, on obtaining the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court, subject to the following conditions:
